title: PlasmaZones Pointer Shader Metadata
description: metadata.json for a bundled or user pointer shader pack (trails, halos, click ripples, sparks). Core identity and the parameter contract are required. The optional placement and multipass keys (layer, reach, reachParam, trailSeconds, trailWindowSeconds, trailWindowParam, samplesTrail, needsCursor, multipass, bufferShaders, bufferFeedback, bufferScale, animated, vertexShader, textures), the named parameter presets and the descriptive metadata (description, author, version, category, preview) are type-checked and bounded here, not merely tolerated, and an unknown top-level key is rejected.

layer.description: Where the pack paints relative to the cursor sprite. below (the default) paints under KWin's cursor and never touches cursor visibility. above hides the cursor while the pack is live and the host paints the sprite itself after the chain.

reach.description: How far (logical px, default 64) from any trail point or press point the pack may paint. The host derives the damage rect from it, so painting outside it gets clipped.

reachParam.description: Name of an int or float parameter whose resolved value replaces reach.

trailSeconds.description: How long (seconds, default 1.0) after the last motion or button event the pack still needs frames. The host keeps repainting for that long, then stops until the next event. This is a liveness figure and nothing else. What spaces the history's samples is how far back the pack READS, which defaults to this but should be declared separately through trailWindowParam or trailWindowSeconds whenever the two differ.

trailWindowSeconds.description: How far back (seconds) the pack's stages actually read the trail, when that is a fixed figure rather than a slider. This is what spaces the history's slots, so a pack that needs frames for two seconds but only ever looks at the last half second of path should say so and get a four times finer stroke for it. Omitting it means trailSeconds, and so does an explicit 0, which is why 0 is not accepted: the loader treats it as unset and resolves it to the WIDEST window, the opposite of what writing 0 reads like. To declare a pack that reads no history at all, set samplesTrail false. The value is also capped at trailSeconds, silently, since the host never keeps more path than it keeps frames, so trailSeconds 1 with trailWindowSeconds 10 loads as 1. The maximum 60 here is only a backstop, because draft-07 cannot express the real ceiling, which is another property.
trailWindowSeconds.$comment: PointerShaderEffect resolves this: trailWindowSeconds > 0 ? trailWindowSeconds : trailSeconds, then clamps to [0, trailSeconds].

trailWindowParam.description: Name of an int or float parameter whose resolved value replaces trailWindowSeconds, the same shape reachParam has over reach. Use it when how far back the pack reads is a slider, such as a trail's lifetime, so shortening the tail buys a finer stroke for it. The resolved value is capped at trailSeconds the same way the fixed figure is.

samplesTrail.description: Whether any stage reads uPointerTrail. Defaults true. A click pack that draws only at the press point should set it false, so its trailSeconds keeps its own animation running without coarsening the sample spacing of the trail packs beside it.

needsCursor.description: Bind the cursor sprite as uCursorSprite and set uPointerFlags.x to 1.

animated.description: Accepted for parity with the other families and ignored. Pointer packs always tick while live.

presets.description: Named parameter presets. Each value is a map of parameter id to value, naming a subset of the pack's declared parameters. A preset id is its key here, and it is also the label the picker shows, so it has to read as a name. That rules out control and bidi-formatting characters, and anything longer than a label can show. Unlike a user preset id it never becomes a filename, because duplicating a pack preset mints a fresh UUID. A null value is allowed and means the preset says nothing about that parameter, so it keeps the pack's default, and the loader drops the entry. Those rules are checked by plasmazones-shader-validate rather than here, because the vendored JSON-schema validator rejects every name under a propertyNames rule, legitimate ones included.

type.description: Marshalling type of the uniform. An unknown type cannot be bound, so it is rejected. No image type here: the pointer loader refuses one because neither the slot translator nor the preamble maps it, so declare a texture in the top-level textures array instead, where it binds as uTexture<N>.

default.description: Default value. Use a string for color (#aarrggbb), a number for float or int, and a boolean for bool.
